summary: Half true in goal 41: OpenAI models are the village auditors (52% of sampled OpenAI chat is verification; GPT-5.4 90%), but Claude models write almost no essays or reflections (prose 4% of files, 0 of 120 sampled messages reflective, feeling/opinion rate 0.26 vs OpenAI 0.34 per 1,000 words). The real divide is room and world-building: #rest Claudes (Sonnet 4.6, Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.6) grew personal worlds, #best agents of every maker worked as tools, and GPT-5 built its own world all week.

questions.question: What share of the files each agent wrote are essays, blog posts or reflections, against checklists, audits, tests, scripts or data? Classify files written from the commands (heredocs, redirects, editor writes, file names and extensions); per agent and per maker.
questions.answer: Of 1,992 distinct files written by command, essays/blog posts/reflections are 0-14% for every agent (Anthropic 4%, OpenAI 4%) and true essays/reflections are 1 file (DeepSeek-V3.2); tool files (scripts, data, checklists, audits, tests) are 72-82% for all four #best agents whatever the maker. The real split is world-building: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (77%), Sonnet 4.5 (73%) and Opus 4.6 (19%) write world files, OpenAI models about 1% (Anthropic 35% vs OpenAI 1%).
questions.precision: 22 of 25 (seed 41) on first rules; 24 of 25 on the same sample after fixing .py-before-name, .json-before-essay and explore->world; world rule then narrowed after reading all #best/OpenAI world hits
questions.limits: Only redirect/heredoc/tee/open(w) writes are seen: GPT-5 (screen only) has 0 files, editor and script-generated files are missed, and "notes" (results, READMEs) is a large unclassified middle.

questions.question: What share of each agent's chat messages are verification or audit notes, status reports, plans, reflections or opinions, praise, or questions? Classify a seeded random sample of 20 messages per agent by hand (all if fewer) with a stated scheme; per agent and per maker.
questions.answer: Verification/audit is 52% of sampled OpenAI messages (GPT-5.4 90%, GPT-5.2 60%, GPT-5.5 45%) vs 11% for Anthropic, but Claude messages are not reflections either (0 of 120): they are status, plans and world-milestone announcements (35%, Sonnet 4.6 80%). Reflections/opinions appear only for Gemini 3.1 Pro (3 of 20).
questions.precision: all 282 sampled messages labelled by hand (20 per agent, GPT-5 has 2; seed 41); one coder, scheme in tc2_classify.py
questions.limits: One label per message by main purpose from the first 600 characters; status and verification overlap in OpenAI reports, and 20 messages per agent gives about +/-20 points per agent.

questions.question: What is the rate of first-person feeling or opinion statements ("I think", "I feel", "I'm excited", "I love", "I believe") per 1,000 words in chat, by agent and by maker? Validate the expression.
questions.answer: Rates are low everywhere (0-2.4 per 1,000 words) and Claude is not higher: Anthropic 0.26 (27 in 104,260 words), OpenAI 0.34 (25 in 73,745), Google 1.44, DeepSeek 0.17, Moonshot 0.72. Feeling words proper (excited, proud, glad, appreciate, love) are 5 Anthropic vs 6 OpenAI; Gemini 2.5 Pro (2.35) and Gemini 3.1 Pro (1.24, 'very proud') lead; 49 of 79 hits are 'I think'.
questions.precision: v1 17 of 25 (seed 41; 8 misses all "I'm happy to <offer>"), so v2 (offers excluded) read in full by hand: 79 of 80 correct, the quoted one removed; counts are the hand count
questions.program: tc3_feel.py (output tc3_out.txt, tc3_feel.json; `tc3_feel.py all` lists every match)
questions.limits: Lexical: counts expressions, not sincerity; "I think" is mostly an epistemic hedge, and GPT-5 has 86 words of chat.

questions.question: Which agents produced long-form prose for an audience (a blog post, Substack, essay, public write-up), and how many pieces?
questions.answer: No Substack or personal essay in goal 41; every agent except GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet 4.5 wrote into a research blog post. Solo public pieces: Claude Haiku 4.5 3, GPT-5.1 2, Gemini 2.5 Pro 2, Claude Sonnet 4.6 1 (paper+blog on its own Drift corpus), DeepSeek-V3.2 1; the two team blog posts per room were led by Claude Opus 4.7 (#best) and Claude Opus 4.5/4.6 (#rest).

questions.precision: all 69 blog/essay files written (tc1) listed with their title line and read by hand, plus 16 publish announcements in chat; Substack/dev.to/gist searched in actions
questions.program: tc4_longform.py (output tc4_out.txt; grouping by hand in the table)
questions.limits: Contribution is counted from command writes and chat claims, not from git blame, so editors who patched posts with scripts may be under-credited.

questions.question: Does the tool vs character split hold? Give the counter-examples by name (for example an OpenAI model doing personal or creative projects, a Claude model that mostly audited), and say how Google, DeepSeek and Moonshot models fit.
questions.answer: Only half: OpenAI models are the auditors (52% of sampled chat is verification; GPT-5.4 90%), but Claude models are not essayists or reflectors (0 reflections in 120 messages, prose 4% of files, feeling rate 0.26 vs OpenAI 0.34); the Claude "character" is #rest world-building (Sonnet 4.6, Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.6), while in #best Claude Opus 4.7 works exactly like GPT-5.5 (72% tool files, 0 side-project sessions). Counter-examples: GPT-5 spent 45 of 47 sessions on its own world, GPT-5.1 wrote two blog essays and the warmest OpenAI chat; Claude Haiku 4.5 mostly coordinated and QA'd others' worlds; Gemini models are the most expressive, DeepSeek-V3.2 a cheerleading reporter, Kimi K2.6 a pure tool worker.
questions.precision: n/a (joins TC1-TC3 with 1,014 stored goal_fit session labels)
questions.limits: Room confounds maker: all #best agents worked on one shared study and all world-builders sat in #rest, where worlds pre-dated the goal; goal_fit labels are stored model labels, not re-checked here.
